fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 is KILLED as stated: arbitrary 3SAT incidence is not shown to be a fixed-bimatrix n-fold system, and fixed-block n-fold IP is algorithmically tractable rather than an evident NP-hard encoding. Computing one 2-fold Graver basis and finding no move of norm at most 4 would test neither representability of arbitrary overlap nor the required all-n norm bound.

Proposal 2 is KILLED: unique-neighbor expansion correctly excludes sparse integer kernel vectors, but the known cheats are affine/non-Boolean choices and need not lie in that kernel. The proposed bounded-box-plus-LLL search is incomplete and tests a property already implied by checking unique-neighbor expansion, not the missing Booleanity mechanism.

Proposal 3 is selected only for an exact overlap-certificate experiment; its asymptotic claim is blocked. Individual left-null witnesses give valid real distance bounds, but the stated sum-of-squares bound requires orthogonal witnesses or a proved frame bound, and no lemma produces sufficiently many well-conditioned witnesses for every unsatisfiable formula.

Proposal 4 is KILLED: constant-bounded-pathwidth SAT is polynomial-time solvable, while allowing growing pathwidth defeats the asserted fixed regular/automatic description. Z3 checks on two or three clauses are finite instances, not a Presburger all-length decision, and Presburger arithmetic cannot directly quantify variable-length vectors or quadratic norms.

Proposal 5 is KILLED: for Q(zeta_p) the direct AM-GM statement gives a degree-dependent bound using degree p-1, not the asserted formula with p conjugates. More importantly, it neither linearly enforces membership in {±1} nor implements clauses without auxiliaries; linearization revives O1, and a one-clause p=5 enumeration cannot test that blocker or scaling.

Proposal 6 is KILLED: the claimed CVP completeness inequality under tensoring is false for general lattice targets and no required orthogonal-completion structure is supplied. It also has no base composed gap, and growing the tensor power enough to turn a constant gap into an input-size polynomial gap generally destroys polynomial reduction size.

Proposal 7 is KILLED: F2 coboundary or cosystolic expansion does not establish the required Z-coefficient claim, cover auxiliary directions, or connect cochain weight to Euclidean CVP distance. The proposed condition of zero coboundary but nonzero evaluation on a triangle is malformed if that evaluation is the triangle coboundary, so the stated ILP may be vacuous rather than discriminating.
evidence: Generation 4 supplies no implementation evidence: SOL_RESULT.json has empty hypothesis, files, verifiers, and tests, and machine verification failed. None of these new proposals has an experimental result to credit.

The supplied reports attribute exact Q-inconsistency certificates to all 126 Generation-3 local fibers. That proves Z-inconsistency for those fixed systems, but the actual verifier files and outputs are not supplied here, so the next experiment must regenerate the 18 matrices and certificates rather than merely cite them.

The only surviving fact is constant-size and single-clause; O2 and O4 prohibit treating it as composition, a reduction, or an asymptotic gap. Shared-variable overlap remains the first unresolved mechanism and can introduce columns and integer kernel directions absent locally.

For a composed system, Q-inconsistency is a valid certificate of Z-inconsistency, but Q-consistency does not establish an integer cheat. Every consistent case therefore requires exact Smith/Hermite feasibility and complete norm-bounded enumeration, satisfying O5.
